# Requirements Analysis draft package

Due November 5, 2026 at 10 p.m. Eastern. Individual assignment.

**Incomplete for final submission: `reflections.pdf` must be written by Timothy and added.** No reflection is generated by the included scripts. Read `AI_ASSISTANCE.md` and review the generated work against the assignment's AI scope before submission.

## Required artifacts included

- `goal_model_Teo.py`, `goal_model_Angela.py`, `goal_model_Rob.py`.
- `goal_model_combined.py`.
- `mermaid.txt`: full combined-model Mermaid Live link, produced by the course framework. The model is embedded in the URL fragment; opening it uses an external website.
- `use_cases.json`: nine cases using the Appendix B fields.
- `matrix.json`: two aligned arrays (2 x P), first use-case/step IDs and then goal IDs.

`goal_catalog.py` and `model_support.py` are required support modules for the four model entry points. `goalmodeling/` is an unmodified local copy of the instructor-linked framework, cached from https://github.com/cmu-relab/goalmodeling on November 4, 2026 (commit `a9fd39b`, full revision recorded in `framework-source.json`). Its classes, edges, refinements, graph generator and link generator are used directly. No package installation is required; Python 3.10.5 or newer is sufficient.

Run any model from this folder, for example:

```bash
python3 goal_model_Teo.py
python3 goal_model_combined.py
```

Each writes Mermaid source and a viewing link under `generated/`. The combined entry point also updates `mermaid.txt`. `python3 build_artifacts.py` rebuilds the JSON files, provenance tables, and review files when working in the original course folder with the source CSVs present. The four model entry points work independently of the original CSV locations.

## IDs, highlighting, and views

- Goal IDs are globally unique in the catalog; the same goal retains its ID between views. Four duplicated IDs are retired in the combined view and explicitly mapped to retained IDs in `goal_catalog.py`.
- Yellow goal nodes and HTML `<mark>` strings in the use-case JSON identify added interpretations. `review/review.html` displays those marks visibly. JSON parsers still read these as ordinary strings.
- Each parent can have multiple refinement objects (OR). Children within one refinement object are conjuncts (AND). Leaf nodes have an assigned software or environment agent.
- Conflict links denote conditional tensions described in `review/analysis.md`; the transcripts do not establish unconditional contradictions.
- `review/diagrams.html` renders all four graphs offline with pan/zoom using the locally cached Mermaid library. Its content-security policy blocks external connections.
- `review/goal_evidence.csv` and JSON contain exact source passages and timestamps. `review/matrix.csv` is the readable two-column transpose of `matrix.json`.

The handout specifies no fixed count of goals or use cases. These drafts use the three locally available stakeholder perspectives and Teo's follow-ups. A fixed inspection retention period, legal ownership rule, or tablet response-time SLA has not been invented.
